sourceInformation.source: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (Parker Brothers, Atari 2600, 1982)
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), TSL and WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub Session Protocol v1, client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural three-band cel shading, ink outlines, faceted glacial scenery and graphic orange/cyan flight instruments
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer with native keyframe clips for walker gait and snowcraft engines; procedural flight banking and physics debris
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated original minor-key score at 10% default volume, synthesized effects and engine/wind ambience, formant-based Animalese-style radio gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world cooperative defense; AI Hub sessions, standalone BroadcastChannel rooms and direct WebRTC connection cards
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted state checks, full automated playthrough, standard-mapping gamepad emulation, touch emulation, offline/live audio analysis, two-page multiplayer and official AI Hub harness; screenshots for visual composition
sourceInformation.research: Read the original scanned 1982 Parker Brothers manual, AtariAge manual transcription, Three.js WebGPURenderer documentation, Rapier scene-query documentation, and AI Hub SDK/client/harness. Verified free flight, advancing walkers, flashing hatches, repair valleys, homing bombs, radar, Force timing and original color/audio presentation.

testingFeedback: 15 confirmed product issues were found and fixed during development verification: four visual issues, ten multiplayer issues, and one graphics-initialization issue. Assertions based on incorrect test assumptions are excluded.
Six were critical: five multiplayer lifecycle or control problems and one intermittent graphics startup failure. All were corrected and covered by subsequent checks.

The full automated three-wave sortie was most helpful: it exposed overly short pacing and then verified about 91 seconds of real flight, 15 walker kills, repairs, resonance, upgrades and all three evacuations.
The blank headless WebGPU screenshot was least helpful. State checks verified WebGPU gameplay, and a WebGL fallback screenshot verified visual composition.
engineFeedback: Three.js makes procedural geometry, TSL cel shading and native animation clips straightforward to combine.

Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank, and concurrent software GPU initialization sometimes failed during fallback. Bounded retries with fresh canvases recovered initialization; the underlying driver trigger is unknown.
The authoritative game simulation, controller-first menus, procedural audio, enemy AI and multiplayer state replication were built for this game.
Coordinating asynchronous WebGPU initialization, Rapier WASM, animation and multiplayer lifecycle required the most care.
none; used the pinned engines without modifications.
Provide reliable fresh-canvas backend fallback and explicit recovery diagnostics in WebGPURenderer.
promptFeedback: The specific source year, controller-first design, attract mode and procedural audio requirements gave the demo a strong identity.
The source name could refer to the film or several games; the 1982 date identifies the original Atari game. Standalone multiplayer has no supplied signaling server, so connection cards were used.
Delivering a complete defense loop, readable TV interface and multiplayer in one portable HTML file was the hardest part.
Specify whether the source year refers to the game or film, and state the preferred standalone multiplayer signaling service if one is available.

aiHub.name: The Empire Bites Frost
aiHub.tagline: Big walkers. Small odds. One very cold day.
aiHub.description: Pilot an ink-shaded snowcraft against towering walkers while three transports escape. Exploit flashing bomb hatches, dodge homing fire, recharge at the repair pad and hold the line alone or with a wingmate.
aiHub.source: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (1982)
aiHub.controls: WASD fly, mouse aim/fire or Space fire, Shift boost, E resonance, Esc pause; pad: left stick fly, right stick aim, R2 fire, L2 boost, Square resonance, Options pause; touch: left/right drag, auto fire.
